prior_findings.note: The current plan, API contract, and T009 consistently set GIT_INDEX_FILE for checkout-index. I ran the documented temporary-index sequence in an isolated repository: it restored target content and the primary index tree hash was unchanged.

The current plan, API contract, and T009 restrict deletion candidates to tracked files, untracked non-ignored files, and configured includeIgnored paths; they explicitly exclude unconfigured ignored paths, and T008 adds a fixture test for this case.

new_findings.summary: The documented hard-crash window leaves a live checkpoint ref without its mandatory journal event, then defers reconciliation outside this feature.
new_findings.evidence: data-model.md:111 requires every checkpoint operation to record an event, but data-model.md:120 explicitly permits a successful `git update-ref` followed by a hard crash before SQLite commit, leaving an orphaned ref with no journal entry and defers reconciliation to Feature 010/M2. This violates FR-007 and the Constitution Article XIII fail-closed / Article III event-coupling requirements stated by the review gate.
new_findings.recommendation: Keep 002 fail-closed by specifying and implementing an in-scope recovery protocol before any checkpoint ref is trusted or acted on (including startup/operation reconciliation of unjournaled refs), or redesign the ordering/storage so a crash cannot leave a usable ref without its event; do not defer this mandatory audit invariant to M2.
